headline: RBI amends NBFC securitisation directions: demat only, ₹1 crore minimum ticket size
summary_points: Securitisation notes must be issued, held and transferred only in dematerialised form.
Minimum ticket size is ₹1 crore at issuance and at every subsequent transfer.
Amortising notes may trade at amortised value even if ticket size falls below ₹1 crore.
Notes issued before April 01, 2027 must also comply with Paras 26 and 27 for transactions.

rows: Demat only; minimum ₹1 crore at issuance and transfers
Can trade at amortised value below ₹1 crore
Size of investment by a single investor
Agreement must require SPE to arrange with registrar, depository, stock exchange etc.
Comply with Regulation 21 of SEBI SDI/SR Regulations, 2008
Transactions in notes issued before April 01, 2027 must comply with Paras 26 and 27

who_is_affected: NBFCs and other originators, SPEs, trustees and investors dealing in securitisation notes under the RBI Securitisation Transactions Directions, 2025.
action_required: Review SPE agreements and note structures, arrange demat and ticket-size controls, and align existing notes' transfers before April 01, 2027.

social.linkedin:
RBI has issued the NBFC (Securitisation Transactions) Amendment Directions, 2026 (RBI/2026-27/306), dated November 23, 2026, effective April 01, 2027.

Key changes to the 2025 Directions:

• Securitisation notes must be issued, held and transferred only in demat form.
• Minimum ticket size of ₹1 crore at issuance and at every subsequent transfer, measured per single investor.
• Amortising notes may trade at amortised value even if below ₹1 crore.
• Originators must ensure the SPE agreement requires arrangements with registrars, depositories and exchanges to enforce the ticket-size rule.
• Public offers must comply with Regulation 21 of the SEBI SDI/SR Regulations, 2008.
• Notes issued before April 01, 2027 are covered for future transactions.

NBFCs, originators and SPEs should review documentation and systems well ahead of the effective date.

Please verify the details with the official RBI notification before acting.
